book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 2 — The First of the Three Spirits
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

iconic_quotes_kept: I am the Ghost of Christmas Past
These are but shadows of the things that have been

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: old miser watching his own past
cast.canonical: a thin bent elderly man, completely bald on top with wispy grey side-hair, a long smooth clean-shaven face and a sharp pointed nose, in a plain striped knee-length nightshirt, barefoot, bare-headed
cast.anchor: thin bent bald clean-shaven old man, sharp nose, striped nightshirt, barefoot
cast.distinct_from: the OLD Scrooge — bald and bare-headed; not the young dark-haired Scrooge

cast.name: Young Scrooge
cast.role: Scrooge as a young man in the memories
cast.canonical: a lean serious young man with a full head of dark hair (NOT bald), clean-shaven, sharp features, a hard ambitious glint starting in his eye, in a plain early-Victorian coat
cast.anchor: lean dark-haired young man, sharp features, hard eyes, plain coat
cast.distinct_from: YOUNG with dark hair — never the old bald Scrooge

cast.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
cast.canonical: a small glowing child-sized spirit in a plain pure-white robe, a single clear candle-flame rising straight up from the very top of its bare head like a little crown of fire, holding a branch of holly with leaves and berries; luminous, both child-like and very old at once; no hat, no staff
cast.anchor: small glowing child-spirit, a flame rising from the crown of its bare head, white robe, holly branch; NO hat, NO staff
cast.distinct_from: not a normal child and not an angel — its one unmistakable mark is the flame growing straight out of the top of its head

cast.name: Fezziwig
cast.canonical: a jovial rotund old gentleman with a big round smiling clean-shaven face under a large curly white old-fashioned wig, a comfortable waistcoat and buckled shoes; no beard, no moustache
cast.anchor: rotund clean-shaven old master, large curly white wig, buckled shoes

cast.name: Belle
cast.canonical: a gentle graceful young woman with a soft kind face and hair in simple ringlets, in a plain modest early-Victorian dress and shawl
cast.anchor: gentle young woman, simple ringlets, plain modest dress and shawl
cast.distinct_from: a young woman — the only principal woman in the stave

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old miser in a nightcap sitting bolt upright in his curtained four-poster bed at midnight as a sudden light floods the room and an unseen hand pulls back the bed-curtains

teen.narration: AS MARLEY HAD WARNED, THE FIRST SPIRIT CAME — WHEN THE CLOCK STRUCK ONE.

bubbles.text: Light flooded the room, and an unseen hand drew back his bed-curtains.

panels.scene: a small glowing child-sized spirit in a plain white robe standing in the dark bedroom, a single candle-flame rising straight up from the top of its bare head, holding a branch of holly, both child-like and strangely old

teen.narration: A STRANGE FIGURE STOOD THERE — LIKE A CHILD, YET SOMEHOW VERY OLD.

bubbles.text: From the top of its head rose a clear jet of light; in its hand it held a branch of holly.

panels.scene: the small glowing child-spirit with the candle-flame rising from the top of its head, white robe, holly branch, speaking gently in the dark bedroom

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: I am the Ghost of Christmas Past.

bubbles.speaker: PAST
bubbles.text: Your past. Rise, and walk with me!

panels.scene: the small glowing child-spirit with the flame on its head leading the old bald nightshirt figure by the hand as they step through a wall out onto an open snowy country road at dawn

teen.narration: ITS GENTLE GRIP COULD NOT BE RESISTED.

bubbles.text: They passed through the wall — and stood on an open country road, the city gone.

panels.scene: the thin bald clean-shaven old man in a striped nightshirt, barefoot, standing in a snowy country lane clasping his hands, moved to wonder, a small village behind

teen.narration: THEY STOOD WHERE SCROOGE HAD BEEN A BOY.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I was a boy here! I could walk this road blindfold.

panels.scene: merry country boys on shaggy ponies trotting down a snowy lane calling to one another, drawn as faint pale see-through shadows, no solid foreground figure

teen.narration: 'THESE ARE ONLY SHADOWS OF THINGS THAT HAVE BEEN,' SAID THE SPIRIT.

bubbles.text: The jolly travellers came on — and could not see or hear them at all.

panels.scene: a single lonely small boy reading by himself at a desk beside a feeble fire in a long, bare, cold schoolroom, no one else there

teen.narration: WHILE THE OTHER BOYS RODE HOME, ONE LONELY BOY WAS LEFT BEHIND AT SCHOOL FOR CHRISTMAS.

bubbles.text: It was Scrooge himself, as he used to be — and the old man wept to see him.

panels.scene: a joyful little girl in a bonnet darting into the bare schoolroom to throw both arms around the lonely boy's neck, both children radiant, an open door behind them
panels.composition: close — little Fan comes for him

teen.narration: HIS LITTLE SISTER FAN CAME TO TAKE HIM HOME.

bubbles.text: 'I've come to bring you home, dear brother — home for good, for ever!' cried little Fan.

panels.scene: a jolly rotund clean-shaven old master with a big round smiling face under a large curly old-fashioned white wig, laughing behind a very high clerk's desk in a warm warehouse office

teen.narration: THE SPIRIT CARRIED HIM ON — TO A WAREHOUSE HE ONCE KNEW: JOLLY OLD FEZZIWIG'S, WHERE YOUNG SCROOGE WAS AN APPRENTICE.

bubbles.text: 'Why, it's old Fezziwig — alive again!' cried Scrooge. 'I was apprenticed here!'

panels.scene: the rotund clean-shaven white-wig master clapping his hands and springing down from his high desk, calling for the warehouse floor to be cleared

teen.narration: HE CLOSED THE SHOP FOR A CHRISTMAS EVE PARTY.

bubbles.speaker: FEZZIWIG
bubbles.text: No more work tonight — it's Christmas Eve! Clear the floor, my lads!

panels.scene: a bright warm warehouse turned ballroom, a fiddler up on the high desk, the rotund white-wig master and many couples dancing under warm lamplight and hanging holly

bubbles.text: In came the fiddler, Mrs Fezziwig, and twenty couples — and away they all went!

panels.scene: the rotund clean-shaven white-wig master and his stout smiling wife dancing a lively reel, his buckled shoes flashing, warm lamplight around them

teen.narration: FEZZIWIG AND HIS WIFE LED THE DANCE.

bubbles.text: Old Fezziwig danced so brightly his buckled shoes seemed to shine like little moons.

panels.scene: the thin bald clean-shaven old man in a striped nightshirt, barefoot, thoughtful and moved, the warm glow of the ballroom fading behind him

teen.narration: THE SPIRIT ASKED WHAT SUCH KINDNESS WAS WORTH.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: A few kind words, a little laughter… Fezziwig made us as happy as if it had cost a fortune.

panels.scene: a gentle young woman with simple ringlets in a plain dress, tears in her eyes, sitting by candlelight beside a lean dark-haired young man whose sharp face has begun to harden with greed
panels.composition: close — Belle and the young Scrooge

teen.narration: YEARS LATER. THE HARD-EYED YOUNG MAN BESIDE HER WAS SCROOGE HIMSELF — AND BELLE, THE GIRL HE HAD LOVED.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: Another idol has taken my place.

panels.scene: the gentle ringletted young woman speaking sadly but steadily; beside her the lean dark-haired greedy-eyed young man looks away, unable to deny it, by candlelight

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: An idol of gold. The love of money has swallowed up everything else in you.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: You fear the world too much.

panels.scene: the gentle ringletted young woman, sorrowful but resolved, half-turning away as if gently releasing someone just out of frame, a plain room around her
panels.composition: single subject — Belle sets him free

teen.narration: SHE GAVE HIM BACK HIS FREEDOM.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: I release you — for the love of the man you once were.

bubbles.speaker: BELLE
bubbles.text: May you be happy in the life you have chosen.

panels.scene: the same young woman, now a gentle matron with simple ringlets, sitting happy by a warm fireside; her children are only soft blurred shapes far behind her

teen.narration: YEARS ON, BELLE SAT HAPPY BY HER OWN FIRESIDE.

bubbles.text: 'I saw an old friend of yours today — Mr Scrooge,' her husband said. 'Quite alone in the world.'

panels.scene: the thin bald clean-shaven old man in a striped nightshirt, barefoot, pressing a large cone-shaped metal candle-snuffer cap down hard with both hands over a brilliant burst of light at his feet, the light still streaming out from under its rim
panels.composition: single subject — Scrooge snuffs the light

teen.narration: UNABLE TO BEAR MORE, SCROOGE TRIED TO PUT THE SPIRIT OUT.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: No more! Show me no more — haunt me no longer!
He forced the snuffer-cap down hard — but the light would not die. And Scrooge knew this was only the FIRST of the three spirits.
